title: Computation of the general split solver
statement: Let $f:\mathbb{N}\to\mathbb{N}$, let $E$ be a finite Turing machine over the Boolean alphabet, and let $T:\mathbb{N}\to\mathbb{N}$ be monotone. Suppose that on every Boolean word $s$, $E$ halts within $T(|s|)$ steps and outputs the binary expansion of $f(|s|)$. Then the machine built from $E$ computes, on every Boolean word $w$, the pairing of the prefix of length $i$ and the remaining suffix when $i$ is the least number satisfying $i+f(i)=|w|$; if no such $i$ exists, it outputs the empty word. Its running time on inputs of length $n$ is at most $20(591+26k)(n+1)(T(n+1)+n+2)$, where $k$ is the number of work tapes of $E$.
hypotheses_covered: $E$ computes the binary expansion of $f(|s|)$ on every Boolean word $s$ within $T(|s|)$ steps
